_names_about: Names on every page (Ümit #4445; logic #4447/#4487/#4517, turkce #4449, Zeki #4448/#4484): the maker's official model name only; open or closed starts the class label; the base model is in the row's details; how we ran a setup is the small grey tag beside the name, 'setting · route · snapshot' (a version that tells two models of one product name apart before the route: 'v1.2 · …'; the leaderboard adds the type, 'chat'/'decision'). The model-level facts (official name, open, base model, snapshot) come from the three sites' shared names file, content/model_names.json (logic's work/model_names.json, 95 models, copied byte for byte, its sha256 pinned here and checked by checks.check_names), looked up by model key (common.model_key: the shown model name without '(…)', lower case, spaces to '-'; name_keys: our key -> the shared file's where it spells it otherwise; the bench-scores.json model_key stays ours). A model it does not list keeps its shown name without '(…)'. The routes below are this site's: the machine a setup on our hardware ran on (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell until the DGX Spark came on 16 Oct; per setup from the players.device timeline of v3.db as branch gpu-cost's content/own_cost.json records it, most-used first, '+' for both), 'API' only where another setup of the same official name ran another way, GPT-6 Luna's 'Decisions API' (Reading's GPT-6 Luna also has a chat API row). By shown setup name; routes_v1 for the v1 set (its own-hardware machine is not on record); a smoke-test, Nackgammon, Learning or 'Did they improve?' setup has none on record. route_words: a setup-name suffix that names the route, left out of the tag where the setup has a route.
